title: Artavon
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Jerusalem Talmud Peah, beginning of chapter 1, folio 3b](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.1.36), and [Bereshit Rabbah, end of chapter 35](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.35.3): Artavlon sent our holy Rabbi one precious pearl, atimiton (great wealth), and Rabbi sent him one mezuzah. Rabbi wrote to him that the mezuzah is more valuable than the pearl, for the pearl he must guard, while the mezuzah guards its owner. [Penei Moshe](https://www.sefaria.org/Penei_Moshe_on_Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.1.1.36.1) explains that he was an important Jew. Hyman judges that the Gaon designated שי״ד in [Erekh Milin, entry Artavan](https://archive.org/details/erekhmilin01rapo/page/n213/mode/2up), rightly identified him as a king of Persia in the time of Antoninus Commodus, the son of Antoninus, Rabbi’s friend.[^1][^2][^3]

Hyman reports that the [Likkut on Zechariah 11](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Nach.578.13) says that Rabbi, Antoninus and Charvan died in one month; Hyman identifies this Charvan as Artavan, who died in the year 504 of the Seleucid era (lishtarot). In [Yoma 11a](https://www.sefaria.org/Yoma.11a.6): “Rabbi Yehudah said: An incident with a certain Artavan” ([Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Yoma.11a.6.1) explains: the man’s name) “who was checking mezuzot in the upper market of Tzippori; a quaestor found him and took a thousand zuz from him.” This Artavon is one particular man, and Hyman infers from the incident that he was an upright Jew.[^4]

notes.text: Peah names Artaban and calls the recipient “our holy Rabbi.” Bereshit Rabbah names Artban and calls the recipient “our master.” Penei Moshe takes Artaban to be an important Jew.

[Hyman’s print, vol. I, p. 243](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/Aaron_Hyman._Toldoth_Tannaim_veAmoraim._I._1910.pdf#page=274) has שי״ר and names the pearl sender Artavon. The supplied Hebrew has שי״ד and Artavlon.

On p. 196 of the linked Erekh Milin, Solomon Judah Löb Rapoport identifies Artaban as a Persian king called Wologeses III. He quotes Charvan from Yalkut, proposes Artaban or Ardaban and argues for December 192 on his own reckoning.

The linked Yalkut names Karbon, king of Persia, alongside Rabbi and Antoninus. Hyman gives Charvan, identifies him with Artavan, and dates his death to 504 of the Seleucid era. The linked Yoma episode calls the mezuzah examiner Artavin. Rashi gives both a personal-name reading and an occupational reading.
